I am currently winding down
the Mastodon bots I used to post sunrise and sunset times
. The precipitating event is that the admin of the instance hosting the associated accounts demanded they be made nigh-undiscoverable, but the underlying cause is that itâs become increasing clear that Mastodon isnât, and wonât ever be, a good platform for âasynchronous ephemeral notifications of any kindâ. Iâd also argue (more controversially) that
itâs simply not good infrastructure for social networking of any kind
. There are lots of interesting people using Mastodon, and Iâm sure it will live on as a good-enough space for certain niche groups. But there is no question that it will never offer the fun of early Twitter, let alone the vibrancy of Twitter during its growth phase. Iâve long since dropped Mastodon from my home screen, and
have switched to BlueSky
for text-centric social media.
Mastodon is an instantiation of
an open standard called ActivityPub
, which was built mainly in reaction to Facebookâs closed ecosystem. In the heady days of the 2010s, there was much resentment of digital monopolies, and many techies dreamed of a way to share posts (among other things; ActivityPub contains data formats for far more than just text and pictures) across their âsocial graphâ without being beholden to a single company. The hostility to any centralized âsource of truthâ that could be owned or co-opted by a single company (the same hostility motivating cryptocurrencies) made âdistributionâ a, perhaps
the
, primary design goal. The distribution model chosen was called âfederationâ: Mastodon would consist of a collection of independent âinstancesâ that were free to âfederateâ together to form (potentially) a single universal social graph.
The important technical point is that ActivityPub is (again, among other things) a protocol for one instance to tell another âI am interested in the following kinds of posts from you, so please send them to me when you see anyâ and for that other instance to periodically say âhere are some posts youâre interested inâ. Obviously thereâs lots of technical detail, but what matters is that itâs
not
(primarily) a mechanism for accessing remote information; itâs a way to asynchronously distribute data so that the data is available
locally
.
Federation does not work
Iâm not saying federation âwonâtâ work or âcanâtâ work. Merely that in 2025, nine years after deployment, federation does not work for the Mastodon use case.
I could opine at length about possible federated architectures and what I think the ActivityPub people clearly got wrong in hindsight.
1
But the proof is in the pudding: Mastodon simply doesnât show users the posts they ask to see, as I quickly learned from my collection of bots.
The most immediate problem is that you only have access to posts that are present on your local instance, and posts are only propagated to your local instance if it has expressed interest in them (to the instance where they originate). Itâs a chicken-and-egg issue: how do you know whether youâre interested in something if you canât see it?
This problem became abundantly clear after setting up my solar bots on the
mas.to
instance: the
mastodon.social
instance (where I keep
my personal account
) had expressed no interest in any of these accounts, so none of their posts were available to my personal account. Crucially, the posts did not exist
even if I visited the profile page of the account
: even after weeks of daily posts, the profile page displayed by mastodon.social claimed the account had never posted, and the posts would only begin appearing after someone on mastodon.social began following the account. (And even then, for reasons far trickier to debug, some posts would never propagate to instances where they did have followers. The ActivityPub architecture and protocol are just flaky.)
The federated model simply abandons the idea of a âsource of truthâ for an account, and as a result it is less reliable (and comprehensible) than mature central-server-with-distributed-caching models used for feeds like
RSS
(as well as every web site).
Account migration does not work
One of the big selling points of Mastodon was that you can pick which instance your account lives on, but it is easy to change your mind and switch to a different instance later on. This feature was
wildly
oversold.
Mastodon allows you to post the equivalent of a web redirect: your followers are informed of your new instance and seamlessly migrated over. Your posts, however, do not move with you. Which is kind of a theme: the system simply doesnât think posts are terribly important.
But worse than that, the redirect is hosted
by your old instance
. If you are moving because your old instance went down, youâre stuck. If you are moving because the administrator of your old instance decided to nuke your account, youâre stuck.

data.title: Remember FastCGI? (2021)
data.author: heavensteeth
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了FastCGI协议及其在现代开发中的适用性。作者将FastCGI与传统的CGI-BIN和无服务器架构进行了比较，指出FastCGI允许进程持久化并处理多个请求，而传统CGI-BIN则为每个请求启动新进程。尽管FastCGI仍在PHP社区中使用，但总体上已不如以前流行。作者尝试用Rust编写一个简单的FastCGI服务器，并使用Nginx进行测试。尽管成功运行，作者认为直接编写HTTP服务器（如使用Rust的Tide框架）更为简便和高效，因为无需额外配置和管理进程。除非处理性能较差或安全性不足的脚本语言，否则直接使用HTTP服务器更为合适。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FastCGI及其相关技术（如SCGI、CGI）的实用性、历史背景和替代方案

不同观点：
• **支持FastCGI的观点**：
  ◦ **ryao**：FastCGI在某些场景下仍然有用，尤其是当脚本语言处理HTTP请求过慢或不安全时。使用现有的FastCGI服务器比自写HTTP服务器更快速和安全。
  ◦ **geenat**：FastCGI服务器（如PHP-FPM）在生产环境中表现出色，支持热重载代码、动态管理worker进程等实用功能。
  ◦ **immibis**：FastCGI作为反向代理和后端之间的协议，具有传递元数据、防止漏洞和请求走私等优势。

• **质疑FastCGI的观点**：
  ◦ **zokier**：FastCGI将简单的文本协议转换为自定义二进制协议，增加了复杂性，且在HTTP1.0时代流行令人困惑。
  ◦ **somat**：直接使用自定义HTTP服务器和代理更为合理，FastCGI的存在和流行可能只是因为名称与CGI的关联性。

• **关于历史背景的观点**：
  ◦ **oso2k**：FastCGI的出现有其历史背景，当时服务器昂贵，进程间切换代价高，FastCGI等技术是对这些问题的优化解决方案。

• **其他协议的讨论**：
  ◦ **NoboruWataya**：SCGI在Gemini协议中比FastCGI更常见，因其简单性受到青睐。
  ◦ **miggol**：类似协议如ASGI在Python中仍然普遍，因其分离关注点和性能优势。

• **具体实现和实例**：
  ◦ **zoobab**：通过Python的cgi-bin支持实现简单的代理。
  ◦ **lmz**：FastCGI还有其他模式/角色，如Authorizer和Filter，尽管实际使用中不常见。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：FastCGI的实用性和复杂性。支持者认为它在特定场景下仍然有用，质疑者则认为直接使用HTTP服务器和代理更为合理。
• **历史背景的重要性**：理解FastCGI在其出现时的技术环境和优化需求，有助于理解其设计和流行原因。
• **其他协议的比较**：讨论中提到了SCGI和ASGI等类似协议，通过比较这些协议的优缺点，进一步探讨了FastCGI的替代方案。

总结：讨论围绕FastCGI的实用性、历史背景和替代方案展开，参与者提供了支持和质疑FastCGI的观点，并讨论了其他相关协议和技术实现。争议的焦点在于FastCGI的复杂性和其在现代技术环境中的适用性。

43620676.article_content:
Remember FastCGI?
27 Jun 2021
rust
“Serverless” is sometimes referred to as “cgi-bin” which isn’t entirely fair as
it’s somewhere between cgi-bin and FastCGI.  Somewhere along the way both faded
from memory. While goofing off last weekend wondered to myself: is
FastCGI
still useful? Unlike the
classic cgi-bin approach where a script or program was executed for each
individual request, FastCGI is a binary protocol which allows for longer lived
processes serving multiple requests. It continues to be used in the PHP
community but seems to have largely fallen out of favor. Nonetheless I decided
to tinker a little bit with FastCGI in Rust.
The most sensible crate that I found was the
fastcgi
and played around a bit.
The crate is a bit old and I needed to do some fiddling to get a simple example compiling:
extern
crate
fastcgi
;
use
std
::
io
::
Write
;
use
std
::
net
::
TcpListener
;
use
log
::
*
;
fn
main
()
->
std
::
io
::
Result
<
()
>
{
pretty_env_logger
::
init
();
let
listener
=
TcpListener
::
bind
(
"127.0.0.1:8010"
)
?
;
info!
(
"Listening on 8010"
);
fastcgi
::
run_tcp
(|
mut
req
|
{
info!
(
"Handling request"
);
for
param
in
req
.params
()
{
info!
(
"{:?}"
,
param
);
}
write!
(
&
mut
req
.stdout
(),
"Content-Type: text/plain
\n\n
Hello, world!"
)
.unwrap_or
(());
},
&
listener
);
Ok
(())
}
In order to test out my little FastCGI server I spun up nginx in Docker which required a little bit of configuration in the
nginx.conf
:
server {
listen 8080;
location / {
include /etc/nginx/fastcgi_params;
fastcgi_pass 127.0.0.1:8010;
}
}
After about 45 minutes of tinkering around I had an end-to-end example working
and arrived at the conclusion that if I was going to do all this process
management and web server configuration, how is this any better than just
running an embedded web server?
A functionally identical Rust program using
Tide
looks something like this:
#[async_std::main]
async
fn
main
()
->
Result
<
(),
std
::
io
::
Error
>
{
tide
::
log
::
start
();
let
mut
app
=
tide
::
new
();
app
.at
(
"/"
)
.get
(|
_
|
async
{
Ok
(
"Hello, world!"
)
});
app
.listen
(
"127.0.0.1:8080"
)
.await
?
;
Ok
(())
}
Unlike the FastCGI version, I can hit this directly when testing and do not require a local web server. Though, if I do wish to put this behind nginx, the configuration is quite similar:
server {
listen 8080;
location / {
proxy_pass 127.0.0.1:8080;
}
}
If you find yourself with a scripted language where processing HTTP requests
might be too slow or unsafe, I can still see some utility for FastCGI. For most
of the rest of us, HTTP won, just write little HTTP webservers.

data.title: Low cost, high speed data acquisition over HDMI [video]
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Steve Markgraf在osmodevcon2024上介绍了如何通过逆向工程，利用廉价的基于Macrosilicon MS2130芯片的USB 3.2 HDMI视频采集器，结合Sipeed Tang nano系列FPGA开发板（每件约10美元），通过HDMI电缆实现低成本、高速的数据采集。这种方法可以将设备用作低成本的高速逻辑分析仪、ADC采集器或自制软件定义无线电（SDR）等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用FPGA板实现USB3接口和外部组件连接的挑战和解决方案

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，便宜的FPGA板由于GPIO引脚数量有限，无法同时连接USB3接口芯片和外部组件（如并行DAC）。这是因为板载连接器占用了GPIO引脚，导致引脚资源紧张。（支持例子：便宜FPGA板的引脚限制问题）

• 另一种观点提出，是否可以通过使用HDMI端口来连接带有USB3芯片的自定义板。这暗示了通过非传统接口（HDMI）实现数据连接的可能性，但也提出了对信号串扰问题的担忧。（支持例子：HDMI端口连接自定义板的潜在可行性与串扰问题）

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了一个技术上的创新（hack），通过重新利用现有端口（如HDMI）来解决引脚不足的限制，显示了在硬件设计中创新思维的重要性。
• 争议焦点在于HDMI端口是否适合用于连接USB3芯片，尤其在信号完整性和串扰方面可能存在的问题。

In the last week, the US Space Force
awarded SpaceX a $5.9 billion deal
to make Elon Musk's space company the Pentagon's leading launch provider, and then it assigned the vast majority of this year's most lucrative launch contracts to SpaceX.
On top of these actions, the Space Force
reassigned the launch of a GPS navigation satellite
from United Launch Alliance's long-delayed Vulcan rocket to fly on SpaceX's Falcon 9. ULA, a joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, is SpaceX's chief US rival in the market for military satellite launches.
Given the close relationship between Musk and President Donald Trump, it's not out of bounds to ask why SpaceX is racking up so many wins. Some
plans floated by the Trump administration
involving SpaceX in recent months have raised
concerns over conflicts of interest
.
Tory Bruno, ULA's president and CEO, doesn't seem too worried in his public statements. In a roundtable with reporters this week at the annual Space Symposium conference in Colorado, Bruno was asked about Musk's ties with Trump.
"We have not been impacted by our competitor's position advising the president, certainly not yet," Bruno said. "I expect that the government will follow all the rules and be fair and follow all the laws, and so we're behaving that way."
It's a separate concern whether the Pentagon should predominantly rely on a single provider for access to space, be it a launch company like SpaceX led by a billionaire government insider or a provider like ULA that, so far, hasn't proven its new Vulcan rocket can meet the Space Force's schedules.
Military officials are unanimous in their answer to that question: "No." That's why the Space Force is keen to add to the Pentagon's roster of launch providers. In the last 12 months, the Space Force has brought Blue Origin, Rocket Lab, and Stoke Space to join SpaceX and ULA in the mix for national security launches.
Results matter
The reason Bruno can say Musk's involvement in the Trump administration so far hasn't affected ULA is simple. SpaceX is cheaper and has a ready-made line of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets available to launch the Pentagon's satellites. ULA's Vulcan rocket is
now certified to launch military payloads
, but it reached this important milestone years behind schedule.
The Pentagon announced Friday that SpaceX, ULA, and Blue Origin
—Jeff Bezos' space company
—won contracts worth $13.7 billion to share responsibilities for launching approximately 54 of the military's most critical space missions from 2027 through 2032. SpaceX received the lion's share of the missions with an award for 28 launches, while ULA got 19. Blue Origin, a national security launch business newcomer, will fly seven missions.
This comes out to a 60-40 split between SpaceX and ULA, not counting Blue Origin's seven launches, which the Space Force set aside for a third contractor. It's
a reversal of the 60-40 sharing scheme in the
last big military launch competition in 2020
, when ULA took the top award over SpaceX.
Space Force officials anticipate Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will be certified for national security missions next year, allowing it to begin winning launch task orders.
Tory Bruno, president and CEO of United Launch Alliance, speaks with reporters at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on May 6, 2024.
Credit:
Paul Hennessy/Anadolu via Getty Images
Bruno said he wasn't surprised with the outcome of this year's launch competition, known as Phase 3 of the National Security Space Launch (NSSL) program. "W
e're happy to get
it," he said Monday.
"I felt that winning 60 percent the first time was a little bit of an upset," Bruno said of the 2020 competition with SpaceX. "I believe they expected to win 60 then ... T
herefore, I believed this time around that they would compete that much harder, and that I was not going to price dive in order to guarantee a win."
While we know roughly how many launches each company will get from the Space Force, the military hasn't determined which specific missions will fly with ULA, SpaceX, or Blue Origin. Once per year, the Space Force will convene a "mission assignment board" to divvy up individual task orders.
Simply geography
Officials announced Monday that this year's assignment board awarded seven missions to SpaceX and two launches to ULA. The list includes six Space Force missions and three for the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO).
SpaceX's seven wins are worth a combined $845.8 million, with an average price of $120.8 million per launch. Three will fly on Falcon 9 rockets, and four will launch on SpaceX's Falcon Heavy.

data.title: China raises tariffs on US goods to 125% and says it won't respond any further
data.author: xnhbx
data.article_summary: 中国宣布将对美国进口商品加征125%的关税，以回应特朗普政府的全球关税政策，贸易战进一步升级。同时，美国对部分中国商品征收高达145%的关税。中国呼吁欧盟共同反对美国的“霸凌”行为，而特朗普则表示仍希望与中国达成协议。由于关税不确定性，欧洲股市下跌，投资者转向黄金等避险资产。中国鼓励消费者购买国产品牌，并表示不会对美方进一步关税做出回应。德国财长表示，若与美国关税谈判失败，欧盟将讨论应对措施。台湾也准备与美国进行关税谈判。总体而言，中美贸易战加剧，全球市场受影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：中美贸易战对全球经济和金融市场的潜在影响

不同观点：
• **tonyedgecombe 的观点**：认为中美之间的商品流通已经停滞，任何试图改善贸易流动的努力都是无意义的。该评论表达了一种悲观态度，暗示当前的局势已经恶化到无法挽回的地步。

• **csomar 的观点**：提出贵金属（如黄金和白银）价格上涨，美国国债利率上升，而美元指数下跌，这种组合情况是前所未有的。Csomar 认为，如果特朗普政府不大幅度调整当前立场，可能会导致全球经济和货币秩序的变革。这暗示了贸易战可能带来的深远影响，并认为需要政治上的调整来避免更大规模的经济变动。

• **suraci 的观点**：简短而乐观，认为在混乱的世界中仍有理性的存在，暗示仍有解决问题的希望和可能性，但没有具体展开论据或举例。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：主要在于中美贸易战的严重性和未来走势。Tonyedgecombe 认为局势已经无可挽回，而 csomar 则认为如果政策调整仍有转机，并提出金融市场可能出现的巨大变化。

• **论据和例子**：Csomar 提供了具体的金融市场数据（如黄金和白银价格、美国国债利率、美元指数）来支持其观点，认为这些变化预示着更大的经济变革。而 tonyedgecombe 没有提供具体数据，但其观点基于对当前贸易流动的观察。

• **讨论关系**：Suraci 的评论更像是一种对 csomar 观点的回应或补充，表达了一种谨慎乐观的态度，而 tonyedgecombe 的观点则与 csomar 形成对比，代表了对现状的更悲观评估。

data.title: Fifty and out: How Gen X became the biggest work losers
data.author: wyclif
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了Gen X一代在创意产业中的兴衰。在1990年代，他们处于行业的巅峰，享受着高薪和奢华生活，比如文章中提到的在迪拜拍摄时 extravagant 的照片拍摄活动。然而，随着数字化时代到来，AI等技术正取代许多他们曾经擅长的职位，如撰稿人、摄影师和设计师。Gen X现在面临年龄歧视和薪水缩水的问题，许多人不得不转行或失业。他们还肩负着同时照顾子女和年迈父母的经济压力。文章通过几个朋友的职业困境，反映了这一代人在当今职场中的失落感和不确定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：媒体对不同代际的关注和刻板印象

不同观点：
• [rsynnott] 认为媒体过去一直关注于抱怨婴儿潮一代和千禧一代，而完全忽视了X世代。他预测，随着媒体编辑逐渐由千禧一代取代，X世代可能会成为新的批评对象，并猜测媒体对X世代的忽视可能是因为当前很多编辑正是X世代。他还幽默地提到，当焦点转向X世代时，有关鳄梨（代指千禧一代对鳄梨吐司的偏好）的讨论将会消失。

• [Clubber] 指出，印刷行业在人工智能出现之前就已经衰落，暗示媒体行业的变化与技术进步有关，而不是仅仅因为代际差异或媒体的关注点转移。

补充讨论：
• [rsynnott] 的评论提到了媒体对代际刻板印象的塑造，并通过推测未来可能出现的X世代刻板印象，反映出对媒体选择性关注某些群体的批评。
• [Clubber] 的评论则将讨论引向技术对传统行业的冲击，暗示媒体讨论的代际问题可能并非行业变化的核心原因。

争议焦点：
• 媒体对不同代际的关注是否公正，是否因为编辑的代际身份影响了对某些群体的刻板印象塑造。

43651228.article_content:
T
rue story. Back in 1999, I was writing a story for a glossy magazine out in Dubai. The country was beginning to shift from oil to tourism. It was prescient – something you might read about in
The Economist
today – but you wouldn’t get the photo shoot that went with it. On the trip was a photographer, his assistant, the lighting guy, someone to play music, some guy for vibes, and a model. It was the Persian Gulf, in the middle of the day with the sun so high in the sky you could blind yourself looking at the water. They were shooting the model deep-sea fishing, so we needed three boats: one for the model, one for the photographer, and one for his extra lights
Obviously, that was ridiculous, but it was the Nineties – nobody worried about the cost of anything, and it was small beer compared to the money being spent by our American counterparts. One friend who moved to New York in the Nineties was paid $5 per word for 5,000-word articles.
Last week,
Vanity Fair
writer Bryan Burrough – author of
Barbarians at the Gate: The Fall of RJR Nabisco
– revealed he’d been paid around $166,000 per feature. “For 25 years, I was contracted to produce three articles a year, typically 10,000 words,” he wrote. “For this, my peak salary was $498,141.”
Ever wonder how Carrie could afford that Manhattan apartment in
Sex and the City
? She was a
Gen X
magazine journalist.
She isn’t now. In the sequel,
And Just Like That…
, she’s the less-famous co-host of a podcast. Miranda, once a lawyer, is studying for a master’s and drinking too much. Charlotte is living vicariously through her daughter. Samantha is awol. And that all tracks with what I see among my friends now.
Recommended
Leave Gen Z alone, Jodie... it’s Gen X you should worry about in the workplace
Kamala Harris identifies as Gen X – and, believe you me, you really don’t want to mess with us
Victoria Beckham has turned 50 – and, believe me, her life is about to get complicated
For a brief moment, Gen X ruled the creative economy, but it was a mirage, and now it feels like we’re losing the plot completely. Take my night out with my mate Ed – an editor of a trade magazine – the other evening: a cheap pint in a pub, bus home, no dinner. The time of living it large at the Met Bar and getting cabs everywhere is a distant memory. This is now a typical Gen X night out.
Together, we ran through what our friends were up to. Andy’s job as a graphic designer has disappeared. Phil, once a highly paid photographer, hasn’t been hired for months, is thinking about getting into Bitcoin, and trying not to panic about how much his divorce is costing him. Alice has had six
jobs
in the past four years. She went from editor to content editor to digital manager to product designer at a laptop company, to something at a car place, to (I think) recruitment. Truthfully, I’m not sure she knows what her job is. A lot of people we know are now “coaches”.
“Each year I stay employed, it’s like I get promoted,” Ed says, after we’d pause to peer into this sliding pit of doom. “I’m paying a guy a fortune to fix my roof. AI isn’t going to fix my roof, but it’s going to take my job.”
It’s no surprise that Generation X – aged between 45 and 59 – are the least satisfied age group at
work
, with 16 per cent believing they do not have a “good” job, according to hiring platform Indeed. Not only are their “talents” often no longer needed in a world where AI is fast replacing copywriters, photographers, and designers, but those still in place often experience age discrimination (around 80 per cent, according to a 2022 AARP survey).
open image in gallery
When it comes to the digital age, Gen-Xers have watched their younger counterparts excel
(
Getty
)
Born in an analogue age, Gen-Xers are watching digital natives leapfrogging them into content creation jobs they don’t understand and are ill-equipped to do, while entire sectors are disappearing overnight. Analysis by the IMF suggests that around 60 per cent of jobs in advanced economies like the UK and US are at risk of being replaced by AI. In the UK alone, AI could displace up to three million private-sector jobs, according to the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change. Many of these are in the creative economy Gen X once thrived in.
This shift is not only having a profound effect on our identity, but also causing a financial meltdown. Gen X were born to the post-war generation, and many of our parents were relatively young when they had us. We then slouched into adulthood with an ironic disregard for convention, meaning we had children later. So now we’re supporting both our university-age kids and our ageing parents in their “care home era” – and doing it on salaries that are rapidly shrinking.

data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 本文由Molson Hart撰写，讨论美国通过提高进口关税试图将制造业带回国内的政策，并指出该政策的14个问题，认为此举难以奏效，甚至可能适得其反。作者拥有15年制造业经验，在中美等多国从事过生产和采购，认为美国制造业成本高昂，供应链不完善，即使加征关税，生产成本仍高于中国。文章指出，美国消费品供应链发达，但工业供应链薄弱，无法满足大规模生产需求。最终，单纯依靠关税无法实现制造业回流，政策制定者需采取更有效的策略。

不同观点：
• 观点一：[anovikov] 认为中国制造业的衰退是不可避免的，主要由于人口结构问题。他预测中国劳动力将出现严重短缺，这会在未来2-3代内发生，可能导致制造业外流。他指出，无论关税政策如何，未来50年内中国将难以找到足够的劳动力，尤其是非技术工人。因此，那些提前开始推动制造业回流的国家或企业将获得优势。

• 观点二：未明确表达但可推断出的潜在观点是，有人可能认为中国可以通过政策调整、技术进步或自动化来缓解人口结构带来的劳动力短缺问题。这种观点强调通过创新和改革来应对挑战，而不是单纯等待衰退。

补充讨论：
• [anovikov] 的评论中提到中国的人口问题不可避免，并暗示其他国家或企业应提前做好准备应对中国制造业的衰退。这一观点的论据主要基于人口统计学和对未来劳动力短缺的预测。

• 争议的焦点在于中国是否能够通过政策措施和技术手段来克服人口结构带来的挑战。有人可能认为通过自动化和技术创新可以缓解劳动力短缺，而[anovikov] 则认为这种短缺是不可逆的，并将对制造业产生深远影响。

• 评论还提到关税问题，暗示无论国际贸易政策如何变化，人口结构问题将对中国制造业产生更深远的影响。这表明在讨论制造业回流时，人口问题可能比关税等政治因素更具决定性。

On April 2nd, 2025, our president announced major new taxes on imports from foreign countries (“tariffs”), ranging from 10% to 49%. The stated goal is to bring manufacturing back to the United States and to “make America wealthy again.”
These tariffs will not work. In fact, they may even do the opposite, fail to bring manufacturing back and make America poorer in the process.
This article gives the 14 reasons why this is the case, how the United States could bring manufacturing back if it were serious about doing so, and what will ultimately happen with this wrongheaded policy
I’ve been in the manufacturing industry for 15 years. I’ve manufactured in the USA and in China. I worked in a factory in China. I speak and read Chinese. I’ve purchased millions of dollars worth of goods from the US and China, but also Vietnam, Indonesia, Taiwan, and Cambodia. I’ve also visited many factories in Mexico and consider myself a student of how countries rise and fall.
In other words, unlike many who have voiced an opinion on this topic, I know what I am talking about. And that’s why I felt compelled to write this article. I had to do it. I’m a first generation American and I love my country and it pains me to see it hurtling at high speed towards an economic brick wall. This article is an attempt to hit the brakes.
The 14 reasons why these tariffs will not bring manufacturing back
They’re not high enough
A tariff is a tax on an imported product. For example, when Apple imports an iPhone that was made in China, it declares to the United States government what it paid to make that product overseas. Let’s say it’s $100. When there is a 54% tariff, Apple pays $100 to the manufacturer in China and $54 to the US government when importing. In this simplified example, an iPhone used to cost Apple $100, but it now costs $154. For every dollar Apple spends, Apple needs to make profit. So Apple sells iPhones to stores for double what it pays for them. And stores sell iPhones to consumers like you and me for double what it pays for them, as well.
Before the tariffs, prices looked like this:
Apple bought iPhones it designed for $100
Apple sold iPhones for $200 to stores
Stores sold iPhones to you and me for $400
After the tariffs, prices look like this:
Apple bought iPhones for $154 ($100 + $54 in import taxes)
Apple sells those iPhones for $308 (double what it paid)
Stores sell those iPhones to you and me for $616 (double what they paid)
Now that you know what a tariff is, let me tell to you why they aren’t high enough to bring manufacturing back to the United States.
In short, manufacturing in the United States is so expensive and our supply chain (we’ll explain that next) is so bad that making that iPhone in the United States without that 54% tariff, would still cost more than in China with 54% tariff. Since it still costs less to make the iPhone in China, both Apple and consumers would prefer it be made there, so it will, and not in the USA.
America’s industrial supply chain for many products is weak
Think of a supply chain as a company’s ability to get the components it needs to build a finished product. Suppose you wanted to build and sell wooden furniture. You’re going to need wood, nails, glue, etc. Otherwise you can’t do it. If you want to build an iPhone you need to procure a glass screen, shaped metal, and numerous internal electronic components.
Now you might be thinking, “What do you mean America has a weak supply chain? I’ve built furniture. I’ve assembled a computer. I can get everything I want at Home Depot and at Amazon.”
That’s because America has an amazing
consumer
supply chain, one of the best, if not the best in the world, but this is totally different from having an
industrial
supply chain.
When you’re operating a furniture factory, you need an industrial quantity of wood, more wood than any Home Depot near you has in store. And you need it fast and cheap. It turns out that the United States has a good supply chain for wood, which is why, despite higher wages, we export chopsticks to China. We have abundant cheap wood in the forests of the Northern United States. But if you decided to move that chopstick factory to desert Saudi Arabia, you would not succeed, because their supply chain for wood is poor; there simply aren’t any trees for 1,000s of miles.
When it comes to the iPhone, all the factories whi

data.article_summary: 本文概述了2025年对话语音AI的现状及其应用，强调了大语言模型（LLM）在对话和将非结构化信息转化为结构化数据方面的优势。语音AI正被广泛应用于医疗、销售、客服、调度等多个商业场景，并在社交应用和游戏中逐渐普及。文章介绍了构建生产级语音代理的复杂性，推荐使用如Pipecat等开源框架来简化开发过程。语音AI代理的基本工作流程包括听取用户语音、进行文本转换和推理、生成回应，并通过语音反馈给用户，目前这些流程主要在云端执行，以确保低延迟和高效能。尽管未来可能更多AI任务会在设备端运行，但当前云端仍是主流。

43649308.article_content:
1. Conversational Voice AI in 2025
LLMs are good conversationalists.
If you've spent much time in free-form dialog with ChatGPT or Claude, you have an intuitive sense that talking to an LLM feels quite natural and is broadly useful.
LLMs are also good at turning unstructured information into structured data.
[1]
New voice AI agents leverage these two LLM capabilities – conversation, and extracting structure from unstructured data – to create a new kind of user experience.
[1] Here we mean this broadly, rather than in the narrow sense of the "structured output" feature of some LLMs.
Voice AI is being deployed today in a wide range of business contexts. For example:
collecting patient data prior to healthcare appointments,
following up on inbound sales leads,
handling an increasing variety of call center tasks,
coordinating scheduling and logistics between companies, and
answering the phone for nearly every kind of small business.
On the consumer side, conversational voice (and video) AI is also starting to make its way into social applications and games. And developers are sharing personal voice AI projects and experiments every day on GitHub and social media.
2. About this guide
This guide is a snapshot of the voice AI state of the art.
[2]
Building production-ready voice agents is complicated. Many elements are non-trivial to implement from scratch. If you build voice AI apps, you'll likely rely on a framework for many of the things discussed in this document. But we think it's useful to understand how the pieces fit together, whether you are building them all from scratch or not.
This guide was directly inspired by Sean DuBois' open-source book
WebRTC For the Curious
. That book has helped numerous developers get up to speed with WebRTC since it was first released four years ago.
[3]
The voice AI code examples in this document use the
Pipecat
open source framework. Pipecat is a vendor-neutral agent layer for realtime AI.
[4]
We used Pipecat in this document because:
We build with it every day and help to maintain it, so we're familiar with it!
Pipecat is currently the most widely used voice AI framework, with teams at NVIDIA, Google, and hundreds of startups leveraging and contributing to the codebase.
We've tried to give general advice in this document, rather than recommend commercial products and services. Where we highlight specific vendors, we do so because they are used by a large percentage of voice AI developers.
Let's get started …
[2] We originally wrote this guide for the AI Engineering Summit in February 2025. We updated it at the beginning of April.
[3]
webrtcforthecurious.com
— WebRTC is relevant to voice AI, as we'll discuss later in the
WebSockets and WebRTC
section.
[4] Pipecat has integrations for more than 50
AI models and services
, along with state of-the-art implementations of things like turn detection and interruption handling. You can write code with Pipecat that uses WebSockets, WebRTC, HTTP, and telephony to communicate with users. Pipecat includes transport implementations for a variety of infrastructure platforms including Twilio, Telnyx, LiveKit, Daily, and others. There are
client-side Pipecat SDKs
for JavaScript, React, iOS, Android, and C++.
3. The basic conversational AI loop
The basic "job to be done" of a voice AI agent is to listen to what a human says, respond in some useful way, then repeat that sequence.
Production voice agents today almost all have a very similar architecture. A voice agent program runs in the cloud and orchestrates the speech-to-speech loop. The agent program uses multiple AI models, some running locally to the agent, some accessed via APIs. The agent program also uses LLM function calling or structured outputs to integrate with back-end systems.
Speech is captured by a microphone on a user's device, encoded, and sent over the network to a voice agent program running in the cloud.
Input speech is transcribed, to create text input for the LLM.
Text is assembled into a context — a prompt — and inference is performed by an LLM. Inference output will often be filtered or transformed by the agent program logic.
[5]
Output text is sent to a text-to-speech model to create audio output.
Audio output is sent back to the user.
You'll notice that the voice agent program is running in the cloud, and the text-to-speech, LLM, and speech-to-text processing are happening in the cloud. Over the long term, we expect to see more AI workloads running on-device. Today, though,
production voice AI is very cloud-centric
, for two reasons:
Voice AI agents need to use the best available AI models to reliably execute complex workflows at low latency. End-user devices do not yet have enough AI compute horsepower to run the best STT, LLM, and TTS models at acceptable latency.
The majority of commercial voice AI agents today are communicating with users via phone calls. For a phone call, there is no end-user device — at least, not one that you can run any code on!

data.title: Photographs of 19th Century Japan
data.author: merothwell
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本旧照片所反映的历史、文化变迁及现代对比

不同观点：
• **canpan** 认为许多历史地点（如Kameido Shrine、Nikko、Osaka Castle等）依然存在，但感慨传统村落景象已不复存在，只有少数地方如Shirakawago保存较好。同时提到现代房屋设计开始重新注重美观。
• **MrRed** 介绍了一个19世纪日本照片的项目，通过与Guimet博物馆的合作，利用技术整理和展示照片，方便用户通过对象检测进行搜索。
• **xandrius** 表示对通过旧照片或旅行记录重新体验过去的世界很感兴趣，认为这有助于理解当前文化及发现被遗忘的小世界。并推荐了一本关于骑行穿越中亚和日本的书。
• **ListeningPie** 对比了不同网站上照片的展示方式，感谢一些网站为用户提供了更好的浏览体验。
• **decimalenough** 提到Nikko的Toshogu Shrine周围景色变化不大，但像Kobe和Nagasaki这样的城市已完全不同。
• **kappasan** 分享了自己在京都一座百年老宅（machiya）工作的经历，虽然环境类似旧照片，但现代便利如便利店已不存在。

补充讨论：
• **potato3732842** 惊叹于看到封建日本的照片，并指出有些人可能活到了1950年代，见证了巨大的社会进步。
• **geokon** 将日本旧照片与宋代的《清明上河图》对比，强调了日本当时相对孤立的状态，像是一个时间胶囊。
• **prmph** 对照片的色彩细节感到惊叹，质疑是否为手工上色，并讨论了如果是手工上色所需的大量工作。
• **throwup238** 提到了与俄罗斯帝国照片的对比，并提供了相关照片资源的链接，同时指出某些照片收藏不易公开访问。
• **helaoban** 对现代世界的变化感到感慨。
• **voidUpdate** 对僧侣服饰的颜色感到惊讶，质疑是否与等级有关。
• **maxtao** 提到宫崎骏的电影《邻居 Totoro》反映了1960年代的日本，并指出一些老年人认为那是景观和现代富裕的最佳结合点。
• **thewileyone** 惊叹于照片中的整洁和有序，认为这是日本文化中的根深蒂固的特征。
• **gramie** 对照片中女孩的笑容感到有趣，指出传统日本文化中女性通常遮掩嘴巴，展示牙齿被认为有些粗俗，但同时也可能受到摄影师的影响。

争议焦点：
• 日本传统村落景象的消失与现代房屋设计的回归美观之间的对比。
• 旧照片中人物服饰和现代认知之间的差异，如僧侣的服饰颜色和女性的笑容。

data.title: Strengths Are Your Weaknesses
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了人的优点和缺点常常是一体两面的现象。作者以自身经历为例，作为一名初级工程师时，他因为快速编码的能力而高效，但也因忽略细节导致生产问题。他指出，团队成员的优点和缺点往往源于同一特质，在不同情境下表现不同。为应对这一问题，作者提出三点建议：

1. 在1对1会议中坦诚讨论这种双重性，帮助员工不再因“缺点”自责。
2. 明确情境，指导员工何时发挥或抑制其自然倾向。
3. 将紧张关系视为一种特性，而非缺陷，通过团队成员互补提升整体表现。

文章强调，管理者的目标不是消除员工的优缺点，而是帮助他们认识并调整这些特质，以适应不同情况。这种理解不仅能提升管理能力，也能让人更加包容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： strengths和weaknesses的关系以及它们在不同情境下的表现和影响

不同观点：
• [w10-1] 认为优点和缺点是相互转化的，特别是在依赖反馈循环的增长过程中。过度依赖某种优点可能会导致忽视其他重要的能力发展，从而形成恶性循环。解决方法是建立明确的成长模型，并愿意为此做出牺牲。

• [agentultra] 认为人不应被简单地归类为具有固定的优点或缺点。优点和缺点是情境性的，可以随着时间和经验改变。人们更倾向于根据具体情境调整自己的表现，而不是被固定的特质所限制。在团队建设中，更应关注成员的价值观和动机，而不是单纯的技能强弱。

• [hliyan] 认为优缺点在特定条件下可能会互相转化，但这种转化不应被提升为普遍原则。人类行为复杂，应根据具体情况进行个案处理，而不是依赖简单的二元分类。

• [the_arun] 认为速度和细节疏忽不是同一特质的两面，而是可以通过协作开发和更好的流程（如代码审查和自动化测试）来最小化风险。强调速度与准确性的结合，以及通过经验积累来提高表现。

• [makeitdouble] 提出一些负面特质（如情感疏离）在特定情况下也可能带来正面影响，例如在组织混乱或工作枯燥时。组织内的多样性也体现在这些特质差异上。

• [zemvpferreira] 分享了个人经历，指出创造力可能与焦虑或躁狂有关，表明优缺点可能在更深层次上相互关联。接受优缺点的共存是成熟的表现。

• [andai] 支持情境依赖的观点，并分享了一个通过具体行为改变来解决负面特质的案例。强调具体反馈和行动计划的重要性。

• [MetaMalone] 认为优点的定义比缺点更难，因为它们非常情境依赖。强调识别当前能力状态的局限性，应更关注如何适应工作需求而不是让工作适应个人。

• [ddawson] 分享了个人经验，指出团队合作可以弥补个人优缺点的局限。通过与他人合作，可以更好地平衡速度与质量。

• [pentamassiv] 引用教授的话，指出生活中的问题总量是恒定的，优点和缺点只是不同情境下的表现。应接受这种平衡，而不是试图完全消除缺点。

• [karmakaze] 质疑全面理解基础设施/技术栈如何能被视为弱点，认为这种观点可能忽视了具体技术实现中的细节和价值。

• [halgir] 以幽默方式指出“工作太努力”是自己的最大弱点。

• [bryanrasmussen] 提到这种优缺点相互转化的观察并不新鲜，并分享了一篇相关文章链接。

• [munificent] 认为优缺点在不同领域和情境下都存在这种相互转化，个人的最大心理挑战往往与带来最大快乐和价值的特质相同。接受这种双面性是一种禅意。

• [ferguess_k] 分享了个人经历，指出自己擅长的事情并非自己喜欢的事情，强调优缺点和个人愿望之间的复杂关系。

补充讨论：
- 优点和缺点在不同情境下的相互转化是一个重要讨论点，强调了情境依赖和个体差异。
- 团队合作和具体行为改变在最小化缺点影响方面的重要性被多次提及。
- 接受优缺点的共存和平衡是多个评论者提到的成熟态度。
- 个人经历和具体案例为讨论提供了丰富的背景和例证。

43652024.article_content:
Your Strengths Are Your Weaknesses
“People are package deals; you take the good with the confused. In most cases, strengths and weaknesses are two sides of the same coin.”
— Steve Jobs
I’ve noticed something interesting about almost every engineer I’ve managed: their biggest strengths and their most frustrating weaknesses are often the exact same trait showing up in different contexts.
I learned this lesson personally when I was still a junior engineer. My ability to code quickly made me very productive — I’d often ship features in half the time estimated. My manager praised my speed constantly.
Well, until one day… During a particularly painful postmortem, we discovered that a production issue happened because of an edge case I had missed in my rush to complete the feature. My strength (coding speed) and my weakness (occasionally overlooking details) weren’t separate traits — they were the exact same characteristic showing up differently depending on the context.
This isn’t just true for me or a few people — it’s nearly universal.
The qualities we celebrate in our team members are usually the same ones causing our biggest headaches
. They’re not separate traits; they’re two sides of the same coin.
So what can we do about this? Three things have helped me:
Get real about this duality in your 1:1s.
Most people see their strengths and weaknesses as separate things. They’re not. In 1:1s, I’ll say something like: “Your ability to dive deep into problems is why you find solutions nobody else can. It’s also why you sometimes miss deadlines. Same trait, different outcomes.” This simple reframing helps people stop beating themselves up over their “flaws.”
Be crystal clear about context.
Don’t make people guess when their natural tendencies help versus hurt. One of my engineers was incredibly collaborative—wouldn’t make a single decision without getting everyone’s input. I told him exactly when this worked and when it didn’t: “For architecture decisions? Get all the input you want. For day-to-day coding decisions? You have permission to just decide and move on.” This clear guidance helped him develop his own judgment about when to lean into his collaborative nature.
Use tension as a feature, not a bug.
Some managers try to build teams where everyone works the same way.
That’s a mistake
. I once paired our fastest coder with our most methodical, thorough reviewer. The first week was pure chaos—they drove each other nuts. By the third week, they were producing better code than either could alone; the fast coder started anticipating the thorough one’s concerns, and the methodical one learned which shortcuts were actually okay to take.
The goal isn’t to create “balanced” engineers with no pronounced strengths or weaknesses. That’s just impossible.
We want self-aware engineers who understand their natural tendencies and can adjust them based on what each situation demands
.
I don’t think our job is to sand down people’s edges until everyone’s the same boring shape. We’re not trying to “fix” our engineers. Instead, we’re helping them see themselves clearly, warts and all, and teaching them when to crank up or dial back their natural tendencies. It’s more like coaching someone to use their power effectively than trying to rebuild them from scratch.
After all, we’re all package deals. The traits that make us brilliant will inevitably challenge us in other contexts. Understanding this doesn’t just make us better managers — it makes us more compassionate humans.

文章强调，管理者的目标不是消除员工的优缺点，而是帮助他们认识并调整这些特质，以适应不同情况。这种理解不仅能提升管理能力，也能让人更加包容。
43652024.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： strengths和weaknesses的关系以及它们在不同情境下的表现和影响

不同观点：
• [w10-1] 认为优点和缺点是相互转化的，特别是在依赖反馈循环的增长过程中。过度依赖某种优点可能会导致忽视其他重要的能力发展，从而形成恶性循环。解决方法是建立明确的成长模型，并愿意为此做出牺牲。

• [agentultra] 认为人不应被简单地归类为具有固定的优点或缺点。优点和缺点是情境性的，可以随着时间和经验改变。人们更倾向于根据具体情境调整自己的表现，而不是被固定的特质所限制。在团队建设中，更应关注成员的价值观和动机，而不是单纯的技能强弱。

• [hliyan] 认为优缺点在特定条件下可能会互相转化，但这种转化不应被提升为普遍原则。人类行为复杂，应根据具体情况进行个案处理，而不是依赖简单的二元分类。

• [the_arun] 认为速度和细节疏忽不是同一特质的两面，而是可以通过协作开发和更好的流程（如代码审查和自动化测试）来最小化风险。强调速度与准确性的结合，以及通过经验积累来提高表现。

• [makeitdouble] 提出一些负面特质（如情感疏离）在特定情况下也可能带来正面影响，例如在组织混乱或工作枯燥时。组织内的多样性也体现在这些特质差异上。

• [zemvpferreira] 分享了个人经历，指出创造力可能与焦虑或躁狂有关，表明优缺点可能在更深层次上相互关联。接受优缺点的共存是成熟的表现。

• [andai] 支持情境依赖的观点，并分享了一个通过具体行为改变来解决负面特质的案例。强调具体反馈和行动计划的重要性。

• [MetaMalone] 认为优点的定义比缺点更难，因为它们非常情境依赖。强调识别当前能力状态的局限性，应更关注如何适应工作需求而不是让工作适应个人。

• [ddawson] 分享了个人经验，指出团队合作可以弥补个人优缺点的局限。通过与他人合作，可以更好地平衡速度与质量。

• [pentamassiv] 引用教授的话，指出生活中的问题总量是恒定的，优点和缺点只是不同情境下的表现。应接受这种平衡，而不是试图完全消除缺点。

• [karmakaze] 质疑全面理解基础设施/技术栈如何能被视为弱点，认为这种观点可能忽视了具体技术实现中的细节和价值。

• [halgir] 以幽默方式指出“工作太努力”是自己的最大弱点。

• [bryanrasmussen] 提到这种优缺点相互转化的观察并不新鲜，并分享了一篇相关文章链接。

• [munificent] 认为优缺点在不同领域和情境下都存在这种相互转化，个人的最大心理挑战往往与带来最大快乐和价值的特质相同。接受这种双面性是一种禅意。

• [ferguess_k] 分享了个人经历，指出自己擅长的事情并非自己喜欢的事情，强调优缺点和个人愿望之间的复杂关系。

补充讨论：
- 优点和缺点在不同情境下的相互转化是一个重要讨论点，强调了情境依赖和个体差异。
- 团队合作和具体行为改变在最小化缺点影响方面的重要性被多次提及。
- 接受优缺点的共存和平衡是多个评论者提到的成熟态度。
- 个人经历和具体案例为讨论提供了丰富的背景和例证。

data.title: Why I Program in Lisp
data.author: ska80
data.article_summary: 本文解释了作者为何偏爱使用Lisp编程，尽管它并不如其他语言流行。Lisp具有简单一致的语法（所有操作均为`(operator operands ...)`格式），减少了记忆和语法困扰。其函数式编程特性支持无副作用的代换模型，允许轻松重构和抽象。Lisp的λ表达式和动态类型使得快速尝试新想法和构建复杂系统更加便捷。通过REPL环境，程序员可以实时评估和调整代码。尽管动态类型可能引入一些隐患，但Lisp的快速原型开发能力和调试便利性使其成为解决问题的理想工具。Lisp的这些特性共同提供了一种高效、有趣的编程体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp语言的优缺点及其实用性

不同观点：
• 一些开发者认为Lisp的括号语法和从内到外的阅读顺序让他们难以适应。例如，[discmonkey]提到Lisp代码的阅读顺序与他习惯的自上而下、从左到右的阅读方式相反，这让他难以完全欣赏这门语言。
• 另一部分开发者则对Lisp持积极态度，认为其强大的表达能力和可定制性使其非常有趣和实用。例如，[djha-skin]指出Lisp的表达力强、易于重构，并且拥有良好的社区支持。
• 有人质疑纯粹函数式编程的实际应用价值，认为I/O操作和设备交互的复杂性使得纯粹函数式编程在实际项目中不太可行。[lukaslalinsky]提出大多数程序都需要处理I/O操作，这与纯粹函数式编程的理念相悖。
• 对于Lisp在生产环境中的使用率低，一些开发者表示疑惑。例如，[bgitarts]提到虽然Lisp经常被称赞，但在生产应用中却很少见。
• 也有开发者对Lisp环境的现代化程度提出质疑，认为现代Lisp环境不如过去的Lisp机器先进，也无法与当前主流的开发工具（如IntelliJ IDEA）竞争。[jll29]具体比较了现代Lisp环境与过去Lisp机器的差距。

补充讨论：
• 一些开发者建议通过具体例子来展示Lisp的优势，例如与Java实现的数独求解器对比，展示Lisp中函数式编程特性（如函数作为数据、递归和宏）的实际应用价值。[smckk]
• 有人提到Lisp的括号语法虽然被一些人诟病，但也有其独特的魅力和价值。[p0w3n3d]引用Terry Pratchett的话幽默地表达了对多重括号的看法。
• 对于Lisp的学习和使用动机，有人表示是为了享受其编程过程中的乐趣和挑战，而不是出于实用性考虑。[dramm]认为编写Lisp博客文章本身也是学习Lisp的一个重要动力。
• 一些开发者分享了他们在实际项目中使用Lisp的经验。例如，[DadBase]提到在过去的项目中使用Lisp编写胶水代码的愉快经历。
• 最后，有人表达了对学习Lisp的兴趣，认为即使不常用，了解Lisp这样的语言也是有价值的。[0xTJ]

争议焦点：
• Lisp的括号语法和阅读顺序是否构成学习障碍和实际使用中的不便。
• 纯粹函数式编程在实际项目中的可行性和价值。
• 现代Lisp环境是否足够先进以支持日常开发需求。

43651576.article_content:
Lisp is not the most popular language.  It never was.  Other
general purpose languages are more popular and ultimately can do
everything that Lisp can (if Church and Turing are correct).  They
have more libraries and a larger user community than Lisp does.
They are more likely to be installed on a machine than Lisp is.
Yet I prefer to program in Lisp.  I keep a Lisp REPL open at all
times, and I write prototypes and exploratory code in Lisp.  Why do
I do this?  Lisp is easier to remember, has fewer limitations and hoops you
have to jump through, has lower “friction” between my
thoughts and my program, is easily customizable, and, frankly, more
fun.
Lisp's dreaded Cambridge Polish notation is uniform and
universal.  I don't have to remember whether a form takes curly
braces or square brackets or what the operator precedency is or some
weird punctuated syntax that was invented for no good reason.  It is (operator
operands ...) for everything.  Nothing to remember.  I basically stopped
noticing the parenthesis 40 years ago.  I can indent how I
please.
I program mostly functionally, and Lisp has three features that
help out tremendously here.  First, if you avoid side effects, it
directly supports the substitution model.  You can tell Lisp
that when it sees this simple form, it can just replace it with that
more complex one.  Lisp isn't constantly pushing you into thinking
imperatively.  Second, since the syntax is uniform and doesn't depend on
the context, you can refactor and move code around at will.  Just
move things in balanced parenthesis and you'll pretty much be
ok.
Third, in most computer languages, you can abstract a specific value by
replacing it with a variable that names a value.  But you can perform a further
abstraction by replacing a variable that names a quantity with a
function that computes a quantity.  In functional programming, you often downplay
the distinction between a value and a function that produces that
value.  After all, the difference is only one of time spent waiting for the
answer.  In Lisp, you can change an expression that denotes an
object into an abtraction that computes an object by simply wrapping
a
lambda
around it.  It's less of a big deal these
days, but properly working
lambda
expressions were only
available in Lisp until recently.  Even so,
lambda
expressions are generally pretty clumsy in other languages.
Functional programming focuses on functions (go figure!).  These
are the ideal black box abstraction:  values go in, answer comes
out.  What happens inside?  Who knows!  Who cares! But you can plug
little simple functions together and get bigger more complex
functions.  There is no limit on doing this.  If you can frame your
problem as "I have this, I want that", then you can code it as a
functional program.  It is true that functional programming takes a
bit of practice to get used to, but it allows you to build complex
systems out of very simple parts.  Once you get the hang of it, you
start seeing everything as a function.  (This isn't a limitation.
Church's lambda calculus is a model of computation based on
functional composition.)
Lisp lets me try out new ideas as quickly as I can come up
with them.  New programs are indistinguishable from those built in to
the language, so I can build upon them just as easily.  Lisp's
debugger means I don't have to stop everything and restart the world
from scratch every time something goes wrong.  Lisp's safe memory
model means that bugs don't trash my workspace as I explore the
problem.
The REPL in lisp evaluates
expressions
, which are the
fundamental fragments of Lisp programs.  You can type in part of a
Lisp program and see what it does immediately.  If it works, you can
simply embed the expression in a larger program.  Your program takes
shape in real time as you explore the problem.
Lisp's dynamic typing gives you virtually automatic ad hoc
polymorphism.  If you write a program that calls +, it will work on
any pair of objects that have a well-defined + operator.  Now this
can be a problem if you are cavalier about your types, but if
you exercise a little discipline (like not defining + on
combinations of strings and numbers, for example), and if you avoid
automatic type coercion, then you can write very generic code that
works on a superset of your data types.  (Dynamic typing is a
two-edged sword.  It allows for fast prototyping, but it can hide
bugs that would be caught at compile time in a statically typed
language.)
Other languages may share some of these features, but Lisp has them all
together.  It is a language that was designed to be used as a tool
for thinking about problems, and that is the fun part of
programming.

data.title: But what if I want a faster horse?
data.author: saeedesmaili
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了科技行业中产品演变的现象。作者以亨利·福特的“更快马”比喻开头，指出许多公司试图创造全新市场，而非仅改进现有产品。然而，作者个人更偏好“更快马”，即更完善的现有服务。以Netflix和Spotify为例，作者批评了它们从简单、用户可控的“快速马”转变成复杂、内容不断变化的“体验平台”。Netflix的推荐算法混乱，内容分类差，用户难以控制自己的观看列表。Spotify也从音乐库变为充斥着不相关内容的平台。整体来看，各类应用正趋向类似TikTok的模式，用户控制权减弱，一致性和用户体验创新下降，反映了“蟹化”式的趋同演变。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技产品和平台的用户体验变化及其背后的商业动机

不同观点：
• **[cjs_ac的观点]**：少数 enthusiasts 对大众品味的影响巨大。通过分析普通用户的反馈来设计产品会导致迎合无明确需求的多数用户，而真正影响舆论的 enthusiasts 却被忽略。这种策略可能会导致产品趋于平庸，但可能是最盈利的模式。
• **[furyg3的观点]**：广告支持的平台越来越像 TikTok，尽管这种变化在逻辑上说得通，但对用户体验不利。例如，LinkedIn 转向广告模式后，作为求职平台的功能受到影响。对于 Netflix 向 "doom-scrolling" 体验的转变则表示困惑，因为订阅模式下，良好的体验应是让用户快速找到喜欢的内容。
• **[dswalter的观点]**：内容许可问题迫使 Netflix 和 Spotify 改变策略，从内容聚合转向自制内容。失去大量内容库的风险迫使它们成为内容生产者，而非仅是聚合者。
• **[WorldPeas的观点]**：对现代软件体验的不满，尤其是对于流媒体服务试图强制推广其流媒体功能。用户期望能够像过去使用 Discman 一样简单地播放本地内容，但现在的软件设计倾向于推送在线内容，忽略了用户的个性化需求。
• **[patapong的观点]**：现代软件变得不如以前令人愉快，过去计算机工具能够快速响应，而现在则常常感觉在和软件的设计者对抗，尤其是当设计倾向于迎合技术水平较低的用户时。
• **[myself248的观点]**：提出 "Tyranny of the Marginal User" 的概念，认为平台为了增长，必须吸引越来越多的用户，即使这些用户并不真正关心或需要该服务。为了在指标上保持增长，平台不得不迎合这些边际用户。
• **[andai的观点]**：认为大规模消费者应用的设计是为普通用户而非技术爱好者设计的。大多数人对于技术的默认行为表示接受，平台利用这种特性来控制和引导用户的消费行为。
• **[ghusto的观点]**：对 Spotify 和 Netflix 的用户界面设计表示不满，认为这些设计没有考虑到用户的实际需求，而是为了推动平台的商业目标。
• **[yakkomajuri的观点]**：数字银行应用在扩展功能时忽略了核心银行服务，导致用户体验变差。平台试图成为 "SuperApp" 却牺牲了基本功能。
• **[Taek的观点]**：问题的根源在于垄断和碎片化，导致用户无法获得过去的内容和服务体验，因为这些都被封闭在不同的平台内。
• **[MortyWaves的观点]**：对现代 UX/UI 设计不满，认为过去的设计更清晰、可用，没有过多的干扰。
• **[jerf的观点]**：建议脱离由指标驱动的平台，自己掌控内容体验。通过本地存储和传统方式获取内容，避免被现代平台的算法控制。
• **[deepsun的观点]**：Spotify 强制推送用户不感兴趣的内容，如未听过的高标题 podcast，尽管用户没有表现出对这些内容的兴趣。
• **[Wowfunhappy的观点]**：流媒体平台的商业动机是让用户对更少或更便宜的内容感到满意，这与购买实体媒介的体验不同，后者更符合用户的利益。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于现代科技平台的设计是否过于迎合普通用户和商业指标，而忽视了 enthusiasts 和个性化需求。
• 讨论还涉及垄断和内容许可对平台策略的影响，以及用户如何通过本地存储等方式重新掌控内容体验。
• 对 "TikTokification" 趋势的不满普遍存在，认为这种趋势对用户体验有害，但平台为了增长和盈利不得不如此。
• 现代软件设计是否应该保留对 power users 的功能和速度支持也是一个讨论重点。

43652723.article_content:
People in tech business circles love this quote by Henry Ford:
If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses.
The idea is to think outside the box and create entirely new markets instead of just new products in existing ones. Like Apple creating the iPhone (sure, smartphones existed before—but cars also existed before the Ford Model T).
But sometimes, I really want a faster horse.
Netflix in 2012 was a super fast horse. It had a simple but massive catalog of movies and shows, solid recommendations, and basic library management. Compared to my limited local media library it was great. You could actively tune your tastes and rate things with a 5-star system.
Netflix today is very different. It’s not a library—it’s an
experience
.
Instead of reliably showing me what I "have" and recommending what I might like, it shuffles content on each interaction, sometimes changing the cover images of shows in real time, like some black-market charlatan. It has no meaningful catalog, no real categories—just short-lived, auto-generated groups like “Binge-worthy” or “Festive spirit.”
Even the “New” section is meaningless. It opens with a “For You” row (huh?), then “Continue Watching”, followed by generic "Popular in
" rows. It feels like YouTube search: ask for something specific, get a few hits, and then a flood of unrelated "popular" and "recommended" content.
“My List” on Netflix randomly shuffles items and changes their covers every few hours. “Continue Watching” may or may not include what I actually watched recently. Sometimes, the engagement algorithms resurrect some random Slovakian cartoon I opened three years ago—one and immediately closed because it that had no English subtitles here in Finland, even though they do exist in other regions.
I just want a faster horse.
Spotify in 2015 was also a super fast horse. It was like my iTunes library, but with millions more tracks. Getting new music became faster, but it didn’t change the nature of my relationship with music.
Spotify today is... basically Netflix. An inconsistent stream of ever-changing content, weak library tools, and an endless barrage of podcasts.
Overall, consistency, user control, and actual UX innovation are in decline. Everything is converging on TikTok—which is basically TV with infinite channels. You don’t control anything except the channel switch. It's like
Carcinisation
, a form of convergent evolution where unrelated crustaceans all evolve into something vaguely crab-shaped.
The list goes on:
YouTube. YouTube: Once a video catalog with social discovery. Now? TikTok.
LinkedIn. Once a network of resumes. Now? TikTok.
Substack. Yeah, a newsletter platform... now launching TikTok-style videos.
Seriously
.
43652723.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了科技行业中产品演变的现象。作者以亨利·福特的“更快马”比喻开头，指出许多公司试图创造全新市场，而非仅改进现有产品。然而，作者个人更偏好“更快马”，即更完善的现有服务。以Netflix和Spotify为例，作者批评了它们从简单、用户可控的“快速马”转变成复杂、内容不断变化的“体验平台”。Netflix的推荐算法混乱，内容分类差，用户难以控制自己的观看列表。Spotify也从音乐库变为充斥着不相关内容的平台。整体来看，各类应用正趋向类似TikTok的模式，用户控制权减弱，一致性和用户体验创新下降，反映了“蟹化”式的趋同演变。
43652723.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技产品和平台的用户体验变化及其背后的商业动机

不同观点：
• **[cjs_ac的观点]**：少数 enthusiasts 对大众品味的影响巨大。通过分析普通用户的反馈来设计产品会导致迎合无明确需求的多数用户，而真正影响舆论的 enthusiasts 却被忽略。这种策略可能会导致产品趋于平庸，但可能是最盈利的模式。
• **[furyg3的观点]**：广告支持的平台越来越像 TikTok，尽管这种变化在逻辑上说得通，但对用户体验不利。例如，LinkedIn 转向广告模式后，作为求职平台的功能受到影响。对于 Netflix 向 "doom-scrolling" 体验的转变则表示困惑，因为订阅模式下，良好的体验应是让用户快速找到喜欢的内容。
• **[dswalter的观点]**：内容许可问题迫使 Netflix 和 Spotify 改变策略，从内容聚合转向自制内容。失去大量内容库的风险迫使它们成为内容生产者，而非仅是聚合者。
• **[WorldPeas的观点]**：对现代软件体验的不满，尤其是对于流媒体服务试图强制推广其流媒体功能。用户期望能够像过去使用 Discman 一样简单地播放本地内容，但现在的软件设计倾向于推送在线内容，忽略了用户的个性化需求。
• **[patapong的观点]**：现代软件变得不如以前令人愉快，过去计算机工具能够快速响应，而现在则常常感觉在和软件的设计者对抗，尤其是当设计倾向于迎合技术水平较低的用户时。
• **[myself248的观点]**：提出 "Tyranny of the Marginal User" 的概念，认为平台为了增长，必须吸引越来越多的用户，即使这些用户并不真正关心或需要该服务。为了在指标上保持增长，平台不得不迎合这些边际用户。
• **[andai的观点]**：认为大规模消费者应用的设计是为普通用户而非技术爱好者设计的。大多数人对于技术的默认行为表示接受，平台利用这种特性来控制和引导用户的消费行为。
• **[ghusto的观点]**：对 Spotify 和 Netflix 的用户界面设计表示不满，认为这些设计没有考虑到用户的实际需求，而是为了推动平台的商业目标。
• **[yakkomajuri的观点]**：数字银行应用在扩展功能时忽略了核心银行服务，导致用户体验变差。平台试图成为 "SuperApp" 却牺牲了基本功能。
• **[Taek的观点]**：问题的根源在于垄断和碎片化，导致用户无法获得过去的内容和服务体验，因为这些都被封闭在不同的平台内。
• **[MortyWaves的观点]**：对现代 UX/UI 设计不满，认为过去的设计更清晰、可用，没有过多的干扰。
• **[jerf的观点]**：建议脱离由指标驱动的平台，自己掌控内容体验。通过本地存储和传统方式获取内容，避免被现代平台的算法控制。
• **[deepsun的观点]**：Spotify 强制推送用户不感兴趣的内容，如未听过的高标题 podcast，尽管用户没有表现出对这些内容的兴趣。
• **[Wowfunhappy的观点]**：流媒体平台的商业动机是让用户对更少或更便宜的内容感到满意，这与购买实体媒介的体验不同，后者更符合用户的利益。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于现代科技平台的设计是否过于迎合普通用户和商业指标，而忽视了 enthusiasts 和个性化需求。
• 讨论还涉及垄断和内容许可对平台策略的影响，以及用户如何通过本地存储等方式重新掌控内容体验。
• 对 "TikTokification" 趋势的不满普遍存在，认为这种趋势对用户体验有害，但平台为了增长和盈利不得不如此。
• 现代软件设计是否应该保留对 power users 的功能和速度支持也是一个讨论重点。

data.article_summary: Roame是一家使用信用卡积分和里程的航班搜索引擎，正在招聘创始产品设计师。该公司获得Y Combinator等顶级投资者的支持，拥有超过100万用户。该职位要求具备3-6年相关经验，擅长UI/UX设计、品牌推广和视频制作。候选人需对旅行、航空和积分有热情，能够独立完成项目并与创始团队紧密合作。工作地点在旧金山，需全职坐班。薪资范围为10万至17.5万美元，股权为0.25%至0.75%。公司提供全面的健康保险、401(k)匹配等福利，并定期组织高端旅行团建。Roame注重努力工作、承担责任和团队合作，鼓励员工积极创新和表达意见，即便存在分歧也能共同推进项目。

We’re seeking a Founding Product Designer with a strong background in UI/UX, visual design, branding, and video production. You’ll have complete ownership of our design strategy and execution, working directly with the CEO and collaborating closely with engineering.

Transform the travel and rewards industry alongside passionate colleagues

We believe that having a strong work ethic is a competitive advantage, and we expect everyone at Roame to put in their best effort when they’re at work.

Our job is to delight our customers, anything to make their lives magical is in line with our mission. We got here because lightning struck the same place multiple times, but not without taking the first step. We can’t resist passion especially when it grows greater than ours.

We can rely on each member of the team to get their work done. When we say we'll do something - we get it done without anyone checking in on us. This way, we can establish a culture of trust and not micromanage each other. We are as strong as our weakest link and we aim to help one another to complete our tasks.
Be Nice

data.title: DDoS Mitigation Leak
data.author: oavioklein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了上周由一家DDoS缓解公司引发的BGP泄漏事件，该事件影响了全球网络。文章解释了BGP泄漏是什么，此次事件的具体情况及其影响，并探讨了RFC 9234中的“仅限客户”BGP路径属性如何有助于防止此类问题。尽管路由卫生已有所改善，限制了泄漏的影响范围，但此次泄漏仍导致了全球互联网流量的短暂中断。文章还提到未来将有关于路由安全现状的网络研讨会，并提供了注册链接。最后，文章呼吁关注BGP失误及其对网络的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DDoS清理中心如何无意中泄露非攻击流量，引发潜在隐私问题，以及互联网拓扑结构对区域网络的集中影响。

不同观点：
• [R4tY9jQ2] 认为DDoS清理中心的BGP路径操纵在试图缓解DDoS攻击时，可能会无意中将合法流量转移到清理中心，从而引发隐私问题。该评论强调了安全解决方案往往伴随着复杂的副作用，尽管其初衷是保护网络安全。

• [groseje] 则关注区域影响，指出互联网拓扑结构会在某些地区造成集中性故障区域，特别是在韩国（40%）和越南（15%）等地区。该评论基于实际设计跨区域互联的经验，强调了在设计网络时需要考虑这些故障区域，并采取相应措施。

补充讨论：
• [R4tY9jQ2] 强调了技术细节，特别是BGP路径操纵如何导致合法流量被错误地重定向，这为隐私问题提供了技术背景。

• [groseje] 提供了实际操作中的例子，说明在设计跨区域网络互联时如何处理这些由互联网拓扑结构引起的集中故障区域，具有实践指导意义。

争议焦点：虽然两者都讨论了网络安全和隐私问题，但[R4tY9jQ2]更侧重于技术实现及其副作用，而[groseje]则更关注实际应用和设计策略。两者从不同角度出发，提供了对同一问题（网络流量异常）的不同层面的理解。

Summary
In this edition of Beyond Their Intended Scope, we take a look at last week’s BGP leak by a DDoS mitigation company which impacted networks around the world. We look at the impacts in both BGP and traffic data, and discuss how RFC 9234’s “Only to Customer” BGP Path Attribute could have helped.
Late last year, we published the first edition of
Beyond Their Intended Scope,
our
new blog series
intended to shed light on BGP mishaps which may have escaped the attention of the internet community but are still worthy of analysis.
In this episode, let’s take a look at a BGP routing mishap from last Tuesday that briefly disrupted and misdirected internet traffic from around the world through Bucharest, Romania, due to a BGP leak by a DDoS mitigation provider.
It may come as a surprise to many that route leaks continue to occur with some regularity. The difference today is that routing hygiene has improved to such a point that these leaks are often contained to the country or region where they originated, limiting the disruption. In this case, route propagation was not limited, but it’s possible the duration of the leak may have been.
The State of Routing Security
Join Doug Madory on April 24 for an in-depth look at the current state of routing security — the progress made and work yet to be done.

These scientists have taken extreme measures to get away from noise.
by
Allison Johnson

see all
Allison Johnson
is a reviewer with 10 years of experience writing about consumer tech. She has a special interest in mobile photography and telecom. Previously, she worked at DPReview.
It’s kind of impossible to grasp the enormity of a cooling tower until it’s suddenly right next to you. Never used for their intended purpose, the cooling towers of Washington Nuclear Projects 3 and 5 (WNP-3 and WNP-5) loom over treetops as I drive up to Satsop Business Park, about an hour and a half outside of Seattle. This abandoned nuclear power plant — a strange mix of massive concrete structures in various states of completion — has been repurposed as an advanced acoustics testing facility.
I visited Satsop on a drizzly day in March to meet Ron Sauro, owner and operator of
NWAA Labs
. Sound-dampening construction materials, noisy washing machines, even the crew cabin of an airplane — these are all things that have passed through the doors of his lab. When companies need to verify how much sound their products make — or how well they dampen sound — they call Ron. I meet him in the parking lot just outside his office and follow him past a sign that states, in no uncertain terms, that I’m entering the premises at my own risk. I make my way into the finished but never-used auxiliary building that would have housed WNP-3’s nuclear reactor.
The auxiliary building that would have housed WNP-3’s reactor is now home to NWAA Labs.
It’s unfortunate that the Washington Public Power Supply System, or WPPSS, chose a name with an acronym that so easily translates to “whoops!” Construction started on WNP-3 and WNP-5, twin nuclear power plants on the same site, in 1977. They ran over budget, and the accident at Three Mile Island in 1979 put a damper on everyone’s enthusiasm for nuclear energy. By 1982, both projects were mothballed, even though WNP-3 was nearly complete.
WPPSS tried to find a buyer in the ’90s, but nobody was in the market for a defunct nuclear power plant. The buildings and land wound up in the hands of the Port of Grays Harbor, which now maintains it as Satsop Business Park. It has hosted
film productions
, an
Overstock.com call center
(now closed), and, at one point,
thousands of recalled VW vehicles
sold back to dealers following an
emissions-cheating scandal
.
Much of the office space seems unoccupied at the moment, and I get the sense that the “business” part of the park never quite took off like the Port was hoping. Most people are unsure what to make of a defunct nuclear power plant, but Sauro isn’t most people.
He and his wife Bonnie opened NWAA Labs in 2010 after convincing the building’s ownership that they could build an acoustics lab in the facility in five months as a proof of concept. Fifteen years later, they’re still operating it out of Satsop, and as far as acoustic lab spaces go, it’s safe to say this one is one of a kind.
To measure how much sound something makes, or how much sound it absorbs, you need a controlled space. Standards organizations including the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) offer strict guidelines for different kinds of acoustical tests. They include specifications for the room the test is carried out in, how much background noise is acceptable, and the instruments used for testing. The job of an acoustics lab is to follow those specifications to guarantee a level of consistency. If Sauro tests a soundproof building material in his lab, you can bet that another lab somewhere else would get nearly the same result. Clients use that information to help inform their designs or ensure that their products conform to standards for noise emissions.
Stepping through the threshold of the auxiliary reactor building, Sauro points out the exterior walls: five feet thick, made of solid concrete and sturdy rebar. I follow him on a curved path marked with yellow lines around the structure that would have housed the reactor; its round cave-like opening is dark and covered by a padlocked fence. A loud rustling by the entrance startles me, and I see a large bird tuck itself into a nook above the door. As we continue into the building, Sauro tells me a cautionary tale of a careless member of a tour group who fell 500 feet down an unfinished elevator shaft and didn’t survive. I focus on keeping between the yellow lines until we reach the building’s elevator — the finished one, that is.

data.title: Why lead is still bad for your brain
data.author: lentoutcry
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了铅对大脑的持久危害，尽管人们已经减少使用铅，但它仍存在于环境中且难以降解。铅是一种重金属，因其耐用和多功能性曾被广泛应用于水管、汽油、化妆品和油漆等产品中。尽管美国自1976年以来血液中的铅含量有所下降，但没有安全的铅暴露水平。铅主要通过肠道和肺进入人体，尤其对儿童影响更大，因为他们的身体更易吸收铅。铅在血液中的半衰期较短，但在软组织和骨骼中可停留多年，并可能重新释放造成损害。孕期和老年时，铅的危害尤为明显。虽然急性铅中毒会导致严重后果，但长期低剂量暴露同样有害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：铅的持续使用及其对健康和环境的影响

不同观点：
• **[londons_explore]** 认为现代社会仍然在许多产品中使用铅，例如屋顶材料、塑料制造、餐具和子弹等，这会导致铅最终进入环境和饮用水源，带来潜在危害。

• **[gregwebs]** 指出有关铅暴露的研究往往低估了问题的严重性，尤其是低水平铅暴露对儿童的影响。虽然法律存在，但对铅污染的监管和执行不力，特别是在儿童用品方面。他建议采取多种措施来减少铅暴露，例如检测铅水平、避免使用旧玩具、选择无铅产品等。

• **[damnitbuilds]** 关心如何检测老房子中的铅暴露问题，特别是针对窗漆和灰尘的铅含量检测，以评估铅对居住在其中儿童的潜在风险。

• **[aziaziazi]** 对铅检测方法提出质疑，尤其是血样检测的有效性，因为铅在体内的半衰期较长，可能在软组织和骨骼中长期残留并造成伤害。

• **[tentacleuno]** 提到小型飞机使用的航空汽油（avgas 100LL）仍然含铅，担心其对健康的潜在影响。

• **[totetsu]** 对铅去除项目的必要性表示关注，并提出对铅影响大脑的长期健康影响的担忧。

• **[Reason077]** 对铅酸电池市场未来几年的增长表示惊讶，并质疑是否真的需要大量开采新铅，因为铅酸电池的高回收率应能减少新铅的需求。

• **[jvanderbot]** 提到加工食品（如婴儿食品）中存在“可接受的铅最低水平”，因为食品加工过程中不可避免会有重金属渗入，质疑社会为何容忍这种情况。

• **[FalseNutrition]** 引用了一篇学术论文，呼吁理性讨论铅暴露问题，并希望通过科学证据来解释铅的危害。

• **[MisterTea]** 指出铅在工业中广泛用于辐射屏蔽，例如电子束处理和粒子加速器实验室中，感叹为了经济利益而忽视铅的危险性。

• **[icameron]** 调侃钓鱼者常用铅制品作为钓坠，暗示实际生活中铅的使用非常普遍。

• **[DonHopkins]** 以讽刺的语气评论那些认为铅不再对大脑有害的人，暗示对铅危害的忽视是显而易见的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于铅暴露的实际危害程度、检测方法的有效性以及社会和法律对铅污染的监管不足。
• 讨论中多次提到儿童特别容易受到铅暴露的影响，建议采取主动检测和预防措施。
• 铅在现代工业中的一些特定用途（如电池、辐射屏蔽）引发了对铅替代品的需求和讨论。
• 铅的开采和使用量问题也是讨论重点，尤其是铅酸电池行业对铅需求的未来趋势。

43651532.article_content:
Why lead is (still) bad for your brain
Wait, wasn’t this solved by the Romans? Anyway, my grandma ate lead paint and she was totally fine.
neuronerd
April 11, 2025
9 minutes
Image credit:
Ionut Stefan
Talking about lead is boring. I would know, I’ve spent quite a bit of time trudging through papers about lead while writing this post and the best opening I could come up with is just how mind-numbingly boring lead is. Sadly, boredom isn’t a good indicator for importance. While the days of enthusiastically throwing lead into whatever we could (from water pipes to gasoline to cosmetics to paints for houses and children’s toys) are over, the lead we’ve pumped into the environment doesn’t give up so easily. And if that wasn’t enough, we’ve still found some use cases to keep it hanging around (why yes, I’m talking about batteries).
Ok, but how bad can it really be? The levels of lead are surely not as high anymore, so it’s not really that dangerous, right? Well… short answer: it’s a bit more complicated. The long answer is the rest of the article.
What is lead?
Lead is a heavy metal. (Little side note: until the writing of this article, I’ve taken the term “heavy metal” pretty much for granted, because everyone knows what a heavy metal is, right? Right? Well… apparently there’s quite a bit of
ambiguity
surrounding the term, but lead is one of the few who meets all of the definitions out there. And heavy typically refers to dense and/or less chemically reactive, i.e. not interested in playing well with others.) So lead is a heavy metal and it’s found naturally in the ground. What makes it pretty neat is that it’s both malleable, but also durable and versatile.
What makes it less neat is that it’s so malleable, versatile, durable, and toxic. As I mentioned in the beginning, lead has been used in a lot of products. And it’s been used since as far back as Roman times. The problem is that lead is so durable, it basically doesn’t degrade. You see, unlike other fun toxic metals, such as mercury (which can be converted in less toxic forms by bacteria), lead is resistant to chemical breakdown, so once you’ve got lead particles in the environment, they will stay there kind of forever, unless you actively remove them somehow. In other words, even if we were to completely stop mining for and using lead (which we aren’t, since the lead-acid battery market is projected to
increase
in the next years), we would still need to deal in a safe manner with what has been put out there.
Of course, since we’ve stopped putting lead in gasoline (and paints, and cosmetics etc.), things have improved. For example, in the US,
levels
of lead in blood samples have markedly
decreased
since 1976. But a decrease doesn’t mean they’ve reached zero. And while many things with negative effects don’t really harm you in small doses, lead isn’t one of them. There is no safe level of lead exposure. What’s more, an average decrease in the US population doesn’t translate into a decrease of the same magnitude across the world, or even across various subgroups of the US population.
Effects of lead and mechanisms behind them
We’ve already established that no amount of lead is safe, but still, the effects of lead exposure on the nervous system don’t occur in an all or nothing manner. They depend strongly both on the level of lead to which one is exposed (more is worse), and the developmental period when exposure occurs (children are more affected than adults).
Lead usually enters the body via one of two routes: either the gut or the lungs. Children absorb more lead than adults because their gut and lung linings are immature compared to adults, allowing more lead to pass through. They also need more iron, calcium, and zinc, metals with which lead is in direct competition (and obviously winning). In addition, small children can be simply more exposed to lead as they have the tendency to put both their unwashed hands, as well as potentially contaminated objects, in their mouths.
While the half-life of lead in the blood (meaning the amount of time needed for the concentration to drop to half) is relatively short, at only 28 days, that’s not the same as the half-life in the body. Some of the lead in the blood will not be eliminated, but it will actually go into the soft tissue, i.e. kidneys, liver, brain, where the half-life is a few months, and more annoyingly, into the bones, where the half-life is between 10 to 30 years. What’s more, from here, lead can leach back into the bloodstream, from where it can once again get into the soft tissue and cause more damage. This happens particularly in pregnancy, thus affecting the unborn babies, but it also occurs during normal ageing, and even more so in conditions such as osteoporosis.
Now, acute effects of lead exposure are pretty clear. If someone were to chomp down on a piece of lead, it would result in seizures, coma, and possibly death. But obviously that’s an unrealistic scenario and not what most people are exposed

data.article_summary: 一名来自英国德比郡的男子 Pete Belton 的纹身意外出现在美国国土安全部（DHS）一份用于识别委内瑞拉犯罪组织 "Tren de Aragua"（TdA）成员的文件中，尽管他与该组织毫无关联。Belton 的纹身是一个纪念女儿出生时间的钟表图案，但这份文件错误地将该图案与其他疑似帮派成员的纹身放在一起。Belton 担心这可能会影响他计划中的美国旅行，甚至可能面临不当指控。尽管美国政府声称其情报评估不仅仅依赖于纹身和社交媒体信息，但已有案例显示有人因纹身被错误地 deported（驱逐出境）。Belton 表示可能会因潜在风险而取消赴美旅行计划。

43652209.article_content:
Media caption,
British manâs tattoo wrongly linked to Venezuelan gang in US government document
Jake Horton
BBC Verify
Published
11 April 2025, 00:08 BST
A tattoo belonging to a man from Derbyshire has appeared in a US government document used to identify members of a notorious Venezuelan gang - despite the man having no connection to the group.
Pete Belton, 44, from Ilkeston says he was shocked to find his forearm featured in a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) document used to help identify alleged members of Tren de Aragua (TdA), a transnational criminal organisation.
"I'm just an average middle-aged man from Derbyshire," he told BBC Verify.
Mr Belton said it was a "bit strange, bit funny at first" but is now worried the family trip he booked to Miami with his wife and daughter in August might end up "being a six month all-inclusive holiday to Guantanamo".
Image source,
Pete Belton
The Trump administration has already deported hundreds of alleged gang members to
a high-security jail in El Salvador
. Lawyers for some of those deportees say they have been incorrectly identified as TdA members based on their tattoos.
Mr Belton's tattoo - a clock face with the date and time of his daughter's birth - was included in a set of nine images for "detecting and identifying" TdA members. Other tattoos featured stars, crowns and a Michael Jordan "jumpman" logo.
"Open source material has depicted TdA members with a combination of the below tattoos," states
the document which appeared in court filings
,
external
.
But reverse image searches show that several of the pictures first appeared on tattoo websites with no obvious links to Venezuela or TdA.
One of them led BBC Verify to an Instagram post by a Nottingham-based tattoo artist who posted about Mr Belton's tattoo nearly a decade ago.
The tattoo image in the DHS document is worse quality than the Instagram post, which was shared in 2016, but it is clearly the same arm and features the same clock face tattoo.
The same image of Mr Belton's tattoo also appeared in a September 2024 report
by the Texas Department of Public Safety
,
external
(DPS) about TdA activity.
BBC Verify contacted both the US DHS and the Texas DPS about the source of the images, but did not receive a response.
But in an email the DHS said it was confident in its law enforcement's intelligence and that its "assessments go well beyond just gang affiliate tattoos and social media."
It's unclear exactly how Mr Belton's tattoo ended up in the US documents, but he's worried about being linked to the gang.
"In my head I'm thinking if I'm working in border force and I saw me walking through I'd think 'hey up we've got one, he's the one in the document'."
He provided multiple images of the tattoo to prove that it's his - and he says that he has no association to the Venezuelan group.
Image source,
Pete Belton
Image caption,
This image shows Mr Belton's tattoo before it was finished in 2016
The US government hasn't deported anyone based on their tattoos alone, according to comments from an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
official in a court filing last month
,
external
.
However, court documents show immigration officials are employing a points-based system known as the
"Alien Enemy Validation Guide"
,
external
to determine if someone is linked to the Venezuelan gang.
It includes a scorecard, and according to the document, eight points across a number of categories could be grounds for arrest or deportation.
Half of these points can be given if a "subject has tattoos denoting membership or loyalty to TdA".
The document says if all eight points come from the symbolism category, which includes tattoos, then further consultation should be taken before designating someone as a member of TdA.
Venezuelan investigative journalist Ronna Risquez, who wrote a book on TdA's origins, said tattoos alone are not evidence of membership.
"TdA does not have tattoos that identifies the gang," she said.
"To confirm whether a person is a member of TdA, authorities must conduct a police investigation to determine whether they have a criminal record. A tattoo, their clothing, or their nationality are not proof."
However, there have been cases where lawyers have argued that people have been wrongfully identified based on their tattoos and were subsequently deported.
US media
,
external
have reported on a man whose lawyers say was deported because of a crown tattoo which was inspired by the Real Madrid football club logo.
Another case saw a makeup artist
,
external
sent to El Salvador after his a crown tattoo with the words "mum" and "dad" was used by US officials as evidence for gang membership, according to his attorneys.
Back in Derbyshire, Mr Belton says his family have considered cancelling their trip to the US due to the potential risks, but they are going to monitor how the story develops.
"Hopefully now they'd realise I'm not a Venezuelan gangster but I've seen crazier things happen in the news recently, so

data.title: Ask HN: Does any one know if Firebase is a successful from Google's perspective?
data.author: pritambarhate
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Firebase的未来前景及是否应使用封闭系统

不同观点：
• 观点一：反对使用封闭系统，如Firebase。用户[999900000999]认为，尽管Google可能不会很快结束Firebase的支持，但由于其封闭源代码性质，迁移到其他服务非常困难。他更偏好使用Render或Heroku等自定义解决方案，因为这些方案让他拥有更多控制权，并且可以开源。他个人从Firebase转到Supabase，最终选择了Django，因为Supabase无法满足其复杂逻辑需求。
  
• 观点二：通过观察SDK和相关项目的活跃度来判断Firebase的稳定性。用户[lbhdc]建议通过查看Firebase的GitHub仓库的活跃度来预测其未来，认为活动平息通常预示着服务可能被终止。根据目前的观察，Firebase的仓库仍有相当多的活动，表明短期内可能不会结束支持。

• 观点三：Firebase作为Google云平台（GCP）的客户获取工具，具有商业价值。用户[spacebanana7]指出，Firebase的存在有助于Google吸引新的企业云客户，这在营销成本高昂的情况下尤为重要。因此，Google有商业动机继续维护Firebase，不像Facebook关闭Parse是因为当时Facebook对云服务没有商业兴趣。

• 观点四：Firebase仍然广泛使用并盈利。用户[OSDeveloper]认为，由于数百家公司仍在使用Firebase并为其带来利润，Google没有理由很快终止该服务。

补充讨论：
• 用户[giorgioz]提到Firebase Studio与AI结合的新动态（通过Instagram上的视频），表明Firebase可能在持续发展和创新，增加了其未来稳定性。

争议焦点：Firebase是否会在未来被Google终止服务，以及使用封闭系统的风险与控制权问题。用户[999900000999]担心迁移困难和控制权缺失，而其他用户则认为Firebase有足够的商业价值和活跃度，短期内不会被终止。

主要讨论点：AI领域中不同工具和平台的发展前景，以及是否需要构建自己的解决方案或依赖现有工具。

不同观点：
• **muzani**：认为Cursor有可能成为AI领域的领先者，类似于Google在搜索引擎领域的成功。同时指出，AI领域仍有其他可以竞争和赢得市场的机会，不同工具（如Manus、ChatGPT Deep Research、Grok）有各自的特性和应用场景，GitHub尝试全覆盖但未成功。

• **ferguess_k**：表达了对构建自己解决方案的强烈兴趣，认为这样做更有意义，并强调了完善的文档和实用视频的重要性。

• **PeterStuer**：认为AI技术的成熟度还处于早期阶段，目前不应过早聚焦于某个主要方向。创新在快速发生，标准化将在未来自然出现。

• **finally4444**：批评现有的AI工具强行应用传统软件原则，认为这不合理。

• **quintes**：通过类比不同编程语言、框架和云服务的存在，认为竞争和多样性是必然的，这有助于社区围绕未来可能的成功技术聚集。

• **stevage**：认为在市场中保留几种选择通常是好事。

补充讨论：
• **tacostakohashi**：引用xkcd漫画（https://xkcd.com/927/），暗示在技术领域中标准化和多样性之间的常见争议和幽默。

争议焦点：
• 是否应在AI领域早期阶段就聚焦于某个主要工具或平台，还是应鼓励多样性和竞争。
• 构建自己的解决方案是否比使用现有工具更有价值。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国出售美国国债（Treasury bonds）的机制及其后续影响

不同观点：
• [nkurz] 对出售美国国债的机制不了解，提出了一系列关于操作流程的问题。他猜测加拿大通过在公开市场出售美国国债获得美元，但对其后如何处理这些美元表示疑问。具体问题包括：这些美元存放在哪里？加拿大是否将美元放入货币市场基金、购买加拿大债券、黄金或股票等？他还关注此操作的次级效应。

• [blitzar] 对该话题涉及的故事持怀疑态度，认为虽然有人声称某些国家在出售美国国债，但没有实际证据支持这些说法。他的观点集中在缺乏事实依据，暗示可能只是传言或未经证实的信息。

• [suraci] 表达了对信息来源不一致的困惑。他提到最初听说中国在出售美国国债，然后消息变成日本，而现在又变成了加拿大。这种信息的不确定性让他感到混乱，暗示不同消息来源之间的矛盾让他难以判断真相。

data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 美国特朗普政府原计划禁止向中国出售Nvidia的高性能AI芯片H20，但在Nvidia CEO黄仁勋出席马尔拉戈庄园的一场晚宴后，政府改变了立场，暂不实施限制。此前，业内预计美国将对H20芯片实施出口管制，因其是美国能合法销往中国的最先进AI芯片。然而，在晚宴后，白宫决定暂缓限制， reportedly 因为Nvidia承诺在美国加大AI数据中心的投资。尽管政治压力增加，但由于商务部相关机构人手不足和政策变动，限制措施被推迟。H20芯片对中国科技公司非常重要，因其在AI模型开发中起到关键作用，而中国目前仍依赖进口此类芯片。

Trump administration backs off Nvidia’s ‘H20’ chip crackdown
The White House was expected to ban sales of the high-performance AI chip to China. Chinese companies had been stockpiling the chip but now the Trump administration is backing off.
Technology
Trump administration backs off Nvidia's 'H20' chip crackdown after Mar-a-Lago dinner
April 9, 2025
11:53 AM ET
By
Emily Feng
,
Bobby Allyn
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang delivers the keynote address at the annual Nvidia GTC conference in San Jose, Calif. last month.
Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption
Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended a
$1 million-a-head dinner
at Mar-a-Lago last week, a chip known as the H20 may have been on his mind.
That's because chip industry insiders widely expected the Trump administration to
impose curbs on the H20
, the most cutting-edge AI chip U.S. companies can legally sell to China, a crucial market to one of the world's most valuable companies.
World
China retaliates with new 84% tariffs as global markets fall
Following the Mar-a-Lago dinner, the White House reversed course on H20 chips, putting the plan for additional restrictions on hold, according to two sources with knowledge of the plan who were not authorized to speak publicly.
The planned American export controls on the H20 had been in the works for months, according to the two sources, and were ready to be implemented as soon as this week.
The change of course from the White House came after Nvidia promised the Trump administration new U.S. investments in AI data centers, according to one of the sources.
Sponsor Message
American lawmakers have been pressuring the Trump administration for weeks to place stricter curbs on cutting edge technology related to artificial intelligence. In February, Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo.,
jointly
called
for export controls on the H20 chip after Chinese tech company DeepSeek
unveiled
a breakthrough AI chatbot that stunned the world in January.
The Trump administration's decision to allow Chinese firms to continue to purchase H20 chips is a major victory for the country, said Chris Miller, a Tufts University history professor and semiconductor expert.
"Even though these chips are specifically modified to reduce their performance thus making them legal to sell to China — they are better than many, perhaps most, of China's homegrown chips," Miller said. "China still can't produce the volume of chips it needs domestically, so it is critically reliant on imports of Nvidia chips."
The White House and the Commerce Department did not return requests for comment. A spokesman for Nvidia declined to comment.
It is unclear if Huang spoke directly to Trump during the Friday event, but two sources say until then, the assumption had been that
Washington's trade war with China
would soon include tight controls on the H20 chip — which were among the chips used by DeepSeek.
The Indicator from Planet Money
Why the US cut China off from advanced chips
Since 2022, U.S. regulators have restricted what semiconductor chips Nvidia can sell to China out of fear that Beijing
could harness
American technology to bolster its AI and military capabilities. The H20 arose under these constraints, becoming the most powerful AI chip it could export to China under the law.
This year, the H20 chip has become increasingly coveted by artificial intelligence companies, because it is
designed
to support
inference
, a computational process used to support AI models like China's DeepSeek and other AI agents being developed by Meta and OpenAI.
Sponsor Message
As a result, the H20 had appeared as if it, too, would be subject to a Trump administration crack down. And tech companies in China responded. In the first three months of the year, leading Chinese tech firms purchased $16 billion worth of H20 chips, The Information
reported
last week, stockpiling the components in anticipation there would soon be U.S. export controls on the chip.
Despite mounting political pressure to broaden American export controls to cover the H20 chip, the regulatory process has encountered delays, in part because of a lack of staff at the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department office responsible for designing and enforcing such controls, according to a third person familiar with the agency's operations who was also not authorized to speak publicly.
BIS has been hobbled by federal cuts and reshuffling under the Trump administration. The country's most senior export control expert, Matthew Boreman,
left
BIS this year as part of an exodus in February of senior agency staff.
President Trump has also moved fast to dismantle and reorganize technology policies implemented by the Biden administration, particularly the CHIPS Act, which
authorized
$39 billion in subsidies for companies to invest in semiconductor supply chains in the U.S.

data.title: Doge Suffers Another Setback, American Oversight Wins Court Order
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 美国监督组织（American Oversight）在针对政府效率部（DOGE）的联邦记录诉讼中取得法院命令，要求DOGE保留所有可能回应信息自由法（FOIA）请求的记录，驳回DOGE关于其延迟保留某些记录已履行法律义务的辩解。法院担忧DOGE的保密问题及其使用加密通讯应用Signal的报道，要求DOGE在指定日期前确认是否所有相关记录已保留。此命令旨在确保透明度和问责制，特别是在埃隆·马斯克即将离开DOGE的背景下。美国监督组织的诉讼旨在测试DOGE是否受FOIA约束，并揭露和阻止马斯克逃避责任和联邦透明度法的行为，同时寻求有关DOGE官员与联邦机构之间通讯的记录及相关潜在利益冲突的信息。
